source.primary_witnesses: Masoretic Text (Hebrew) per BHS Codex Leningradensis B19A (1008 CE) — the standard Hebrew Bible critical text. Daniel 1 is entirely Hebrew (the Hebrew-Aramaic transition occurs later at 2:4b). SECONDARY: 4Q112 (Daniela, late 2nd c. BCE — the oldest Daniel witness) preserves fragments of Dan 1; 1Q71 (Daniela, 1st c. BCE) preserves fragments. TERTIARY: Old Greek (OG, Codex Chisianus + Papyrus 967) + Theodotion-Greek (Codex Vaticanus + Alexandrinus) per Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Hebrew SBL/Sefaria convention with Tiberian vocalization (ḥ ṣ ʿ; macrons for long vowels ā ē ī ō ū; ə for shewa). Aramaic uses parallel SBL conventions for Imperial/Biblical Aramaic.
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + Ulrich et al. DJD XVI 2000 codicology + Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS Codex Leningradensis (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia Daniel; Goldingay 1989 WBC Daniel; Hartman-Di Lella 1978 AB; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Charles 1929; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.citation: Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich, E., et al., 'Daniel' in Qumran Cave 4 XI (DJD XVI, Oxford 2000); Collins, J. J., Daniel: A Commentary (Hermeneia, Minneapolis 1993); Goldingay, J. E., Daniel (WBC 30, Dallas 1989); Hartman, L. F., and Di Lella, A. A., The Book of Daniel (AB 23, 1978); Newsom, C. A., and Breed, B. W., Daniel (OTL, Louisville 2014); Montgomery, J. A., A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Book of Daniel (ICC, Edinburgh 1927; PD); Charles, R. H., A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Book of Daniel (Oxford 1929; PD); Ziegler, J., and Munnich, O., Susanna, Daniel, Bel et Draco (Septuaginta XVI.2, Goettingen 1999).
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 1 — HEBREW, the court-tale prologue (Daniel + the three companions at Nebuchadnezzar's court). Establishes the wisdom-court frame. 4Q112 preserves fragmentary material of this chapter (frags 1-2); the MT is the primary witness throughout. The Hebrew of chapter 1 is late Biblical Hebrew (LBH) with characteristic features (Persian loanwords, Aramaisms) consistent with a 6th-2nd c. BCE compositional range; Collins 1993 favors a 2nd c. BCE Maccabean-era final form for the apocalyptic chapters with the court tales (1-6) representing earlier diaspora-tradition material. The chapter establishes the dietary-faithfulness and divinely-granted-wisdom themes that frame the entire book.

verses.text: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹשׁ לְמַלְכ֖וּת יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה בָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶֽיהָ׃
verses.translit: bi-šnat šālōš lə-malkūt Yəhōyāqīm melek-Yəhūdāh bāʾ Nəbūkadneʾṣṣar melek-Bābel Yərūšālaim wa-yāṣar ʿālêhā
verses.witness_secondary: 4Q112 frag 1 line 1 (fragmentary) — opening of the book; per Ulrich DJD XVI 2000 p. 252
verses.notes: **INCIPIT — In the third year of Jehoiakim's reign, Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem and besieged it.** **CHRONOLOGICAL CRUX**: this dating (third year of Jehoiakim) conflicts with Jer 25:1 + Jer 46:2 (which dates Nebuchadnezzar's Carchemish campaign to Jehoiakim's fourth year). Collins 1993 + Newsom 2014 treat this as either: (a) Babylonian regnal-year reckoning (where the accession year is year 0), or (b) a deliberate literary-chronological scheme distinct from Jeremiah. The siege itself: 605 BCE per most reconstructions. Persian loanwords appear in this chapter (פַּרְתְּמִים partemim 'nobles' v.3 from Old Persian fratama-) — a key dating-indicator.

verses.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י בְּיָד֜וֹ אֶת־יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֗ה וּמִקְצָת֙ כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיְבִיאֵ֥ם אֶֽרֶץ־שִׁנְעָ֖ר בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהָ֑יו וְאֶת־הַכֵּלִ֣ים הֵבִ֔יא בֵּ֖ית אוֹצַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
verses.translit: wa-yittēn ʾădōnāy bə-yādō ʾet-Yəhōyāqīm melek-Yəhūdāh ū-miqṣāt kəlê bêt-hā-ʾĕlōhīm wa-yəbīʾēm ʾereṣ-Šinʿār bêt ʾĕlōhāyw wə-ʾet-ha-kēlīm hēbīʾ bêt ʾōṣar ʾĕlōhāyw
verses.notes: **The Lord gave Jehoiakim into his hand, with some of the vessels of the house of God; he brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and put the vessels into the treasury of his god.** **TEMPLE-VESSELS MOTIF**: introduces the vessels that will return in Dan 5:2-4 (Belshazzar profanes them) — narrative-arc closure. 'Land of Shinar' (אֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר) archaically denotes Babylonia — same toponym as Gen 10:10 + 11:2 (Tower of Babel). The geographic-mythic resonance frames Babylon as the same site of arrogant city-building.

verses.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְאַשְׁפְּנַ֖ז רַ֣ב סָרִיסָ֑יו לְהָבִ֞יא מִבְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וּמִזֶּ֥רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה וּמִן־הַֽפַּרְתְּמִֽים׃
verses.translit: wa-yōʾmer ha-melek lə-ʾAšpənaz rab sārīsāyw lə-hābīʾ mi-bənê Yiśrāʾēl ū-mi-zeraʿ ha-məlūkāh ū-min-ha-partəmīm
verses.notes: **The king commanded Ashpenaz the chief of his eunuchs to bring some of the Israelites of royal seed and of the nobility.** **KEY LOANWORD**: פַּרְתְּמִים (partəmīm) from Old Persian *fratama- 'foremost ones, nobles' — a Persian loanword indicating a post-exilic / Persian-period compositional layer at minimum for the final form. cf. Esth 1:3, 6:9 (same word). The eunuch-court framing (rab sārīsāyw) raises the question (treated by Daniel-1 rabbinic tradition) whether the four young men were themselves castrated — see Isa 39:7 prophecy.

verses.text: יְלָדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵֽין־בָּהֶ֣ם כָּל־מאוּם֩ וְטוֹבֵ֨י מַרְאֶ֜ה וּמַשְׂכִּילִ֣ים בְּכָל־חָכְמָ֗ה וְיֹ֤דְעֵי דַ֙עַת֙ וּמְבִינֵ֣י מַדָּ֔ע וַאֲשֶׁר֙ כֹּ֣חַ בָּהֶ֔ם לַעֲמֹ֖ד בְּהֵיכַ֣ל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּֽלְלַמְּדָ֥ם סֵ֖פֶר וּלְשׁ֥וֹן כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
verses.translit: yəlādīm ʾăšer ʾên-bāhem kol-məʾūm wə-ṭōbê marʾeh ū-maśkīlīm bə-kol-ḥokmāh wə-yōdəʿê daʿat ū-məbīnê maddāʿ wa-ʾăšer kōaḥ bāhem la-ʿămōd bə-hêkal ha-melek ū-lə-lammədām sēper ū-ləšōn kaśdīm
verses.notes: **Young men without blemish, handsome, skillful in all wisdom, endowed with knowledge, understanding learning, competent to serve in the king's palace; they were to be taught the literature and language of the Chaldeans.** **THE WISDOM-COURT FRAME**: the four-fold wisdom-vocabulary (ḥokmāh + daʿat + maddāʿ + sēper) anticipates the wisdom-gift theme of Dan 1:17. 'Language of the Chaldeans' (ləšōn kaśdīm): the cuneiform-Akkadian scribal tradition; sets up Daniel's expertise in mantic interpretation. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. the Joseph-at-Pharaoh's-court typology (Gen 41) — Daniel is being framed as a new Joseph.

verses.text: וַיְמַן֩ לָהֶ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֗וֹ מִפַּת־בַּ֤ג הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וּמִיֵּ֣ין מִשְׁתָּ֔יו וּֽלְגַדְּלָ֖ם שָׁנִ֣ים שָׁל֑וֹשׁ וּמִ֨קְצָתָ֔ם יַֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.translit: wa-yəman lāhem ha-melek dəbar-yōm bə-yōmō mi-pat-bag ha-melek ū-mi-yên mištāyw ū-lə-gaddəlām šānīm šālōš ū-mi-qəṣātām yaʿamdū li-pnê ha-melek
verses.notes: **The king assigned them daily portions of his royal rations and of the wine he drank; they were to be educated for three years, then enter the king's service.** **KEY LOANWORD**: פַּת־בַּג (pat-bag) from Old Persian *patibāga- 'royal portion / royal table-share' — diagnostic Persian-period vocabulary. The three-year education sets up the dietary-test that begins in v. 8.

verses.text: וַיְהִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם מִבְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה דָּנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָֽה׃
verses.translit: wa-yhī bāhem mi-bənê Yəhūdāh Dāniyyēʾl Ḥănanyāh Mīšāʾēl wa-ʿĂzaryāh
verses.notes: **Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah of the tribe of Judah.** **THE FOUR NAMES — all YHWH/EL-theophoric Hebrew names**: Daniel (דָּנִיֵּאל 'El is my judge'), Hananiah (חֲנַנְיָה 'Yah has been gracious'), Mishael (מִישָׁאֵל 'who is what El is'), Azariah (עֲזַרְיָה 'Yah has helped'). The contrast with their Babylonian renaming in v. 7 — substituting Babylonian deity-names — is theologically pointed.

verses.text: וַיָּ֧שֶׂם לָהֶ֛ם שַׂ֥ר הַסָּרִיסִ֖ים שֵׁמ֑וֹת וַיָּ֨שֶׂם לְדָֽנִיֵּ֜אל בֵּ֣לְטְשַׁאצַּ֗ר וְלַֽחֲנַנְיָה֙ שַׁדְרַ֔ךְ וּלְמִֽישָׁאֵ֣ל מֵישַׁ֔ךְ וְלַעֲזַרְיָ֖ה עֲבֵ֥ד נְגֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wa-yāśem lāhem śar ha-sārīsīm šēmōt wa-yāśem lə-Dāniyyēʾl Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar wə-la-Ḥănanyāh Šadrak ū-lə-Mīšāʾēl Mêšak wə-la-ʿĂzaryāh ʿĂbēd Nəgō
verses.notes: **The chief of the eunuchs gave them new names: Daniel → Belteshazzar; Hananiah → Shadrach; Mishael → Meshach; Azariah → Abednego.** **THE BABYLONIAN NAMES**: Belteshazzar likely from Akkadian *Bēlet-šar-uṣur 'O lady, protect the king' or *Balāṭsu-uṣur 'protect his life'; Shadrach + Meshach are uncertain (possibly distorted theophorics with Babylonian deities Marduk + Aku); Abed-nego = ʿAbd-Nabū 'servant of Nabu' (the Babylonian wisdom-god). **The renaming is an act of cultural assimilation; the dietary refusal in vv. 8-16 is the counter-act of cultural-religious resistance.**

verses.text: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם דָּנִיֵּאל֙ עַל־לִבּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יִתְגָּאַ֛ל בְּפַתְבַּ֥ג הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וּבְיֵ֣ין מִשְׁתָּ֑יו וַיְבַקֵּשׁ֙ מִשַּׂ֣ר הַסָּרִיסִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א יִתְגָּאָֽל׃
verses.translit: wa-yāśem Dāniyyēʾl ʿal-libbō ʾăšer lōʾ-yitgāʾal bə-patbag ha-melek ū-bə-yên mištāyw wa-yəbaqqēš mi-śar ha-sārīsīm ʾăšer lōʾ yitgāʾāl
verses.notes: **Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's rations or his wine; he asked the chief of the eunuchs for leave not to defile himself.** **DIETARY-FAITHFULNESS THEME** — the foundational diaspora-Jewish-identity narrative. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Tob 1:10-11 (Tobit refuses Gentile food in diaspora); cf. Jdt 12:1-4 (Judith refuses Holofernes' food); cf. 1 Macc 1:62-63 (Maccabean martyrs refuse defiling food); cf. 2 Macc 6:18-7:42 (Eleazar + the seven brothers). The motif crystallizes Jewish identity-resistance in the Hellenistic crisis.

verses.text: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־דָּ֣נִיֵּ֔אל לְחֶ֖סֶד וּֽלְרַחֲמִ֑ים לִפְנֵ֖י שַׂ֥ר הַסָּרִיסִֽים׃
verses.translit: wa-yittēn hā-ʾĕlōhīm ʾet-Dāniyyēʾl lə-ḥesed ū-lə-raḥămīm li-pnê śar ha-sārīsīm
verses.notes: **God granted Daniel favor and compassion before the chief of the eunuchs.** **DIVINE-FAVOR FRAME**: closely parallels Joseph (Gen 39:21 — same idiom 'YHWH gave Joseph favor in the eyes of the prison-keeper'). Daniel-as-Joseph typology is sustained throughout chs 1-2.

verses.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר שַׂ֤ר הַסָּרִיסִים֙ לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל יָרֵ֤א אֲנִי֙ אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִנָּ֔ה אֶת־מַאֲכַלְכֶ֖ם וְאֶת־מִשְׁתֵּיכֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֡ר לָמָּה֩ יִרְאֶ֨ה אֶת־פְּנֵיכֶ֜ם זֹֽעֲפִ֗ים מִן־הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּגִֽילְכֶ֔ם וְחִיַּבְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־רֹאשִׁ֖י לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.translit: wa-yōʾmer śar ha-sārīsīm lə-Dāniyyēʾl yārēʾ ʾănī ʾet-ʾădōnī ha-melek ʾăšer minnāh ʾet-maʾăkalkem wə-ʾet-mištêkem ʾăšer lāmmāh yirʾeh ʾet-pənêkem zōʿăpīm min-ha-yəlādīm ʾăšer kə-gîləkem wə-ḥiyyabtem ʾet-rōʾšī la-melek
verses.notes: **The chief eunuch said: 'I fear my lord the king who has appointed your food and drink; should he see your faces leaner than the other youths of your age, you would endanger my head with the king.'** The official's risk-aversion sets up the test-proposal of vv. 11-14.

verses.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר דָּנִיֵּ֖אל אֶל־הַמֶּלְצַ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִנָּה֙ שַׂ֣ר הַסָּרִיסִ֔ים עַל־דָּנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָֽה׃
verses.translit: wa-yōʾmer Dāniyyēʾl ʾel-ha-melṣar ʾăšer minnāh śar ha-sārīsīm ʿal-Dāniyyēʾl Ḥănanyāh Mīšāʾēl wa-ʿĂzaryāh
verses.notes: **Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.** **TERM**: הַמֶּלְצַר (ha-melṣar) — a hapax-like title, possibly from Akkadian *maṣṣaru 'guard, watchman' or from a Persian source; Collins 1993 favors Akkadian etymology.

verses.text: נַס־נָ֥א אֶת־עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ יָמִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֑ה וְיִתְּנוּ־לָ֜נוּ מִן־הַזֵּרֹעִ֛ים וְנֹאכְלָ֖ה וּמַ֥יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
verses.translit: nas-nāʾ ʾet-ʿăbādêkā yāmīm ʿăśārāh wə-yittənū-lānū min-ha-zērōʿīm wə-nōʾkəlāh ū-mayim wə-ništeh
verses.notes: **'Test your servants for ten days; let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.'** **TEN-DAY TEST**: the diet of זֵרֹעִים (zērōʿīm 'seeds, vegetable-things, pulses') and water — a Levitically-safe minimal diet. Foundational vegetarian-dietary-resistance text in the Hebrew Bible; cited in modern Jewish + Christian + Adventist vegetarian-discipline traditions.

verses.text: וְיֵרָא֤וּ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ מַרְאֵ֔ינוּ וּמַרְאֵה֙ הַיְלָדִ֔ים הָאֹ֣כְלִ֔ים אֵ֖ת פַּתְבַּ֣ג הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּרְאֵ֔ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה עִם־עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃
verses.translit: wə-yērāʾū lə-pānêkā marʾênū ū-marʾēh ha-yəlādīm hā-ʾōkəlīm ʾēt patbag ha-melek wə-ka-ʾăšer tirʾeh ʿăśēh ʿim-ʿăbādêkā
verses.notes: **'Then let our appearance and the appearance of the youths who eat the king's rations be examined before you; deal with your servants according to what you see.'**

verses.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע לָהֶ֖ם לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְנַסֵּ֖ם יָמִ֥ים עֲשָׂרָֽה׃
verses.translit: wa-yišmaʿ lāhem la-dābār ha-zeh wa-yənassēm yāmīm ʿăśārāh
verses.notes: **He listened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.**

verses.text: וּמִקְצָת֙ יָמִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֔ה נִרְאָ֤ה מַרְאֵיהֶם֙ ט֔וֹב וּבְרִיאֵ֖י בָּשָׂ֑ר מִן־כָּל־הַיְלָדִ֔ים הָאֹ֣כְלִ֔ים אֵ֖ת פַּתְבַּ֥ג הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.translit: ū-mi-qəṣāt yāmīm ʿăśārāh nirʾāh marʾêhem ṭōb ū-bərīʾê bāśār min-kol-ha-yəlādīm hā-ʾōkəlīm ʾēt patbag ha-melek
verses.notes: **At the end of ten days they appeared better and fatter than all the youths who ate the king's rations.** **NARRATIVE VINDICATION**: the dietary-faithfulness produces physical superiority — a polemical inversion of the assumption that the king's table is the optimal diet.

verses.text: וַיְהִ֣י הַמֶּלְצַ֗ר נֹשֵׂא֙ אֶת־פַּתְבָּגָ֔ם וְיֵ֖ין מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְנֹתֵ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם זֵרְעֹנִֽים׃
verses.translit: wa-yhī ha-melṣar nōśēʾ ʾet-patbāgām wə-yên mištêhem wə-nōtēn lāhem zērəʿōnīm
verses.notes: **So the steward took away their rations and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables.**

verses.text: וְהַיְלָדִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אַרְבַּעְתָּ֔ם נָתַ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם הָֽאֱלֹהִ֛ים מַדָּ֥ע וְהַשְׂכֵּ֖ל בְּכָל־סֵ֣פֶר וְחָכְמָ֑ה וְדָנִיֵּ֣אל הֵבִ֔ין בְּכָל־חָז֖וֹן וַחֲלֹמֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: wə-ha-yəlādīm hā-ʾēlleh ʾarbaʿtām nātan lāhem hā-ʾĕlōhīm maddāʿ wə-haśkēl bə-kol-sēper wə-ḥokmāh wə-Dāniyyēʾl hēbīn bə-kol-ḥāzōn wa-ḥălōmōt
verses.notes: **To these four youths God gave knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.** **DIVINELY-GRANTED-WISDOM THEME**: the foundational program-statement of the book — Daniel's mantic-interpretive gift (חָזוֹן + חֲלוֹם 'vision + dream') is from God, not Chaldean training. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Joseph (Gen 41:16 'not I; God will give Pharaoh a favorable answer'); cf. Joseph (Gen 41:38-39 'a man in whom is the spirit of God'); cf. 1 Kgs 3:9-12 (Solomon's wisdom-gift). Daniel-as-Joseph + Daniel-as-Solomon typology converges.

verses.text: וּלְמִקְצָת֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־אָמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לַהֲבִיאָ֑ם וַיְבִיאֵם֙ שַׂ֣ר הַסָּרִיסִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י נְבֻכַדְנֶצַּֽר׃
verses.translit: ū-lə-miqṣāt ha-yāmīm ʾăšer-ʾāmar ha-melek la-hăbīʾām wa-yəbīʾēm śar ha-sārīsīm li-pnê Nəbukadneṣṣar
verses.notes: **At the end of the time the king had set for their presentation, the chief of the eunuchs brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.**

verses.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתָּם֮ הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וְלֹ֤א נִמְצָא֙ מִכֻּלָּ֔ם כְּדָנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָ֑ה וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.translit: wa-yədabbēr ʾittām ha-melek wə-lōʾ nimṣāʾ mi-kullām kə-Dāniyyēʾl Ḥănanyāh Mīšāʾēl wa-ʿĂzaryāh wa-yaʿamdū li-pnê ha-melek
verses.notes: **The king spoke with them; none of them all was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they entered the king's service.**

verses.text: וְכֹ֗ל דְּבַר֙ חָכְמַ֣ת בִּינָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בִּקֵּ֥שׁ מֵהֶ֖ם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַֽיִּמְצָאֵ֞ם עֶ֣שֶׂר יָד֗וֹת עַ֤ל כָּל־הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ הָֽאַשָּׁפִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּכָל־מַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-kōl dəbar ḥokmat bīnāh ʾăšer-biqqēš mēhem ha-melek wa-yimṣāʾēm ʿeśer yādōt ʿal kol-ha-ḥarṭummīm hā-ʾaššāpīm ʾăšer bə-kol-malkūtō
verses.notes: **In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king inquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in all his realm.** **TERMS**: חַרְטֻמִּים (ḥarṭummīm 'magicians, ritual specialists' — from Egyptian ḥry-tp; same word as Gen 41:8 Pharaoh's magicians) + אַשָּׁפִים (ʾaššāpīm 'enchanters' from Akkadian āšipu 'incantation-priest'). The four Hebrew youths surpass the entire Mesopotamian mantic establishment — wisdom-court polemic.

verses.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל עַד־שְׁנַ֥ת אַחַ֖ת לְכ֥וֹרֶשׁ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.translit: wa-yhī Dāniyyēʾl ʿad-šənat ʾaḥat lə-Kōreš ha-melek
verses.notes: **Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus.** **CHRONOLOGICAL FRAME**: Daniel's tenure extends through the Persian conquest (539 BCE). The notice frames the book's chronological span — exile-court through Persian-restoration. Note however Dan 10:1 places a Daniel vision in 'the third year of Cyrus,' creating a small internal tension typically resolved as 'first year of Cyrus' meaning the inception of Daniel's special-end-time prophetic activity. cf. 2 Chr 36:22, Ezra 1:1 (first year of Cyrus = the return-decree).
